answer_key.title: Rubeus Elevated ASKTGT CreateNetOnly
answer_key.description: This dataset represents adversaries crafting raw AS-REQ (TGT request) traffic for a specific user and encryption key (/rc4, /aes128, /aes256, or /des) to request TGTs without touching lsass.

verdict.assessment: An operator used Rubeus to request a Kerberos TGT for domain user pgustavo using a pre-obtained RC4 hash, then created a new logon session with those credentials. The operator also attempted to access sensitive processes (winlogon, LSASS) for credential extraction.

findings.name: AS-REP Roasting
findings.behavior: Rubeus.exe requested a Kerberos TGT for user pgustavo using a known RC4 hash (81d310fa34e6a56a31145445891bb7b8), triggering a TGT request on the domain controller with RC4 encryption.
findings.reasoning: Rubeus.exe used the /asktgt parameter with a known RC4 hash to request a TGT for pgustavo without requiring the user's password, which is characteristic of AS-REP roasting when preauthentication is disabled. The RC4 encryption type (0x17) in the TGT request and the hash-based authentication method distinguish this from golden ticket forgery, which would require the KRBTGT hash instead.

findings.name: LSASS Memory
findings.behavior: Rubeus.exe accessed winlogon.exe and LSASS-related processes with full access rights (0x1f3fff), attempting to extract credentials from protected system processes.
findings.reasoning: Rubeus.exe opened winlogon.exe with full access rights (0x1f3fff), a characteristic pattern of LSASS credential dumping tools attempting to access protected system processes that hold cached credentials. The access mask and target process are consistent with credential extraction from LSASS memory rather than registry-based secrets or cached domain credentials.

findings.name: Make and Impersonate Token
findings.behavior: A new logon session (LogonType=9) was created for user wardog using the /netonly flag, establishing a credential impersonation context with the stolen pgustavo credentials.
findings.reasoning: The event shows a new logon session (LogonType=9) created for user wardog, which is the signature of runas /netonly creating a new token for credential impersonation. This matches T1134.003 (Make and Impersonate Token) as it demonstrates the creation of a new logon session/token rather than spawning a process with an existing token.
